investigation.title: project-agent-a2a-roundtrip: Planner agent halts after list_agents — send_to_agent never invoked, reviewer receives zero events
investigation.summary: The desktop-release eval for project-agent-a2a-roundtrip failed because the planner agent called list_agents successfully but never proceeded to call send_to_agent, leaving delivered, targetMatches, and reviewerAckObserved all false. The reviewer agent received zero events and its event-wait timed out after 120 000 ms, confirming no A2A message was dispatched during the 143 494 ms run.
investigation.rootCause: The root cause is uncertain but is localized to the send_to_agent dispatch step within the agent-to-agent routing layer on desktop-release. The planner agent completed the agent-discovery phase (list_agents returned results, listAgentsUsed=true, parentCallbackObserved=true) but stopped before issuing send_to_agent. This points to a failure in the planner's decision or tool-invocation logic after agent discovery — either the send_to_agent tool is unavailable or misconfigured in the planner's tool set, the planner's model response after list_agents did not produce a send_to_agent tool call, or the A2A routing/delivery layer silently dropped or rejected the dispatch. The sibling failure of project-agent-subagent-roundtrip (context hydration broken) suggests a broader issue with inter-agent communication infrastructure on this runtime, but the two checks have distinct failure signatures and no shared error message, so a single shared dependency failure is not confirmed by the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: project-agent-subagent-roundtrip: Post-completion context hydration timed out — contextUtilization=0, subagentContextCount=0
investigation.summary: The subagent lifecycle completed successfully (subagentSpawned=true, subagentCompleted=true, subagentReturnedMarker=true, expectedReply=SUBAGENT_PROBE_OK), but the post-turn context hydration step never populated: contextUtilization remained 0 and subagentContextCount remained 0, with the probe recording a 45-second timeout error. This is an eval failure localized to the context-hydration polling phase of the runProjectSubagentRoundtrip function, not a failure of the subagent execution path itself.
investigation.rootCause: After the subagent turn completed, the eval probe's context-hydration wait loop timed out after 45000ms without receiving a non-zero contextUtilization or any subagentContextCount entries. The subagent stream frames (subagent_spawned, subagent_status, tool_result) all arrived and the marker was returned, indicating the execution path is healthy. The failure is isolated to the post-turn context read-back: either the context/usage data is not being written back to the parent agent's context store after a subagent turn completes, the API endpoint or event that the probe polls for context hydration is not emitting the expected update within the 45-second window, or the probe's polling logic in runProjectSubagentRoundtrip is targeting a stale or incorrect context key. Root cause is uncertain between a runtime regression in context write-back and a probe-side polling defect; additional source inspection of runProjectSubagentRoundtrip is required to distinguish them.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps at all.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, meaning the peer-pod VM slot quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of the eval run. The other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules and were therefore ineligible. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 133–146 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval runner timed out and reported failure. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval run.

investigations.title: project-agent-a2a-roundtrip: Planner agent halts after list_agents — send_to_agent never invoked, reviewer receives zero events
investigations.summary: The desktop-release eval for project-agent-a2a-roundtrip failed because the planner agent called list_agents successfully but never proceeded to call send_to_agent, leaving delivered, targetMatches, and reviewerAckObserved all false. The reviewer agent received zero events and its event-wait timed out after 120 000 ms, confirming no A2A message was dispatched during the 143 494 ms run.
investigations.rootCause: The root cause is uncertain but is localized to the send_to_agent dispatch step within the agent-to-agent routing layer on desktop-release. The planner agent completed the agent-discovery phase (list_agents returned results, listAgentsUsed=true, parentCallbackObserved=true) but stopped before issuing send_to_agent. This points to a failure in the planner's decision or tool-invocation logic after agent discovery — either the send_to_agent tool is unavailable or misconfigured in the planner's tool set, the planner's model response after list_agents did not produce a send_to_agent tool call, or the A2A routing/delivery layer silently dropped or rejected the dispatch. The sibling failure of project-agent-subagent-roundtrip (context hydration broken) suggests a broader issue with inter-agent communication infrastructure on this runtime, but the two checks have distinct failure signatures and no shared error message, so a single shared dependency failure is not confirmed by the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: project-agent-subagent-roundtrip: Post-completion context hydration timed out — contextUtilization=0, subagentContextCount=0
investigations.summary: The subagent lifecycle completed successfully (subagentSpawned=true, subagentCompleted=true, subagentReturnedMarker=true, expectedReply=SUBAGENT_PROBE_OK), but the post-turn context hydration step never populated: contextUtilization remained 0 and subagentContextCount remained 0, with the probe recording a 45-second timeout error. This is an eval failure localized to the context-hydration polling phase of the runProjectSubagentRoundtrip function, not a failure of the subagent execution path itself.
investigations.rootCause: After the subagent turn completed, the eval probe's context-hydration wait loop timed out after 45000ms without receiving a non-zero contextUtilization or any subagentContextCount entries. The subagent stream frames (subagent_spawned, subagent_status, tool_result) all arrived and the marker was returned, indicating the execution path is healthy. The failure is isolated to the post-turn context read-back: either the context/usage data is not being written back to the parent agent's context store after a subagent turn completes, the API endpoint or event that the probe polls for context hydration is not emitting the expected update within the 45-second window, or the probe's polling logic in runProjectSubagentRoundtrip is targeting a stale or incorrect context key. Root cause is uncertain between a runtime regression in context write-back and a probe-side polling defect; additional source inspection of runProjectSubagentRoundtrip is required to distinguish them.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps at all.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, meaning the peer-pod VM slot quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of the eval run. The other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules and were therefore ineligible. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 133–146 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval runner timed out and reported failure. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval run.
